name: Mount Daniel and Mount Hinman
region: Alpine Lakes Wilderness, Cle Elum River headwaters

legs.route: West Ridge (class 2); ski parties also climb it by the Foss Glacier

legs.connect: Leave Hinman by its northeast shoulder, drop across glacier slabs to the tarns and Pea Soup Lake, then climb the ridge southwest of the lake to reach the Lynch Glacier. The two summits cannot be joined along the ridge between them.

how: Climbers camp in the high basin near Pea Soup Lake or up by the peaks and take the two summits on separate pushes, in either order. There is no walkable crest between them: the cliffs on Daniel's west side are rotten, so the link goes down to Pea Soup Lake and back up. Late in summer the Lynch Glacier carries crevasses and bare ice, and the snowfield below it can force class 3–4 scrambling on the rock beside it. In spring the same pair is done on skis.
descent: Most parties retrace their steps over the Daniel summit area or down to Pea Soup Lake, then follow the approach out. Ski parties use the Foss and Lynch glaciers for the downhill.
logistics: The approach starts from the Cle Elum River road and runs by Tucquala Meadows; in spring the road can hold snow before its end. The lake may still be frozen early in the season. Crampons and an ice axe are needed on the Lynch Glacier.
notes: Redo of a dropped entry. Evidence: one summer Hinman west ridge to Pea Soup Lake to Daniel traverse (class 2 and class 3 as given in that trip header), plus three ski trips by two parties doing both peaks. Evidence is ski-heavy. No trailhead name or approach trail number was confirmed, so none is stated. SummitPost, Mountaineers and WTA returned 403.

name: Little Annapurna and McClellan Peak

legs.route: Gully and ridge from the notch beside The Prong, with third and fourth class scrambling

legs.connect: Descend the short snowfield back from the notch, then traverse west across the basin toward Crystal Lake and climb straight up Little Annapurna.

duration: 1 long day, or 2–3 days from a camp
how: Both summits sit above the core Enchantment basin and are usually taken on one outing, either in a long day through the core or from a camp. Coming from Snow Lake, McClellan comes first: cross-country past Leprechaun Lake, a short steep snowfield to the notch by The Prong, then a ridge scramble that includes third and fourth class moves. Little Annapurna is the steeper walk but not technical. Campers often add Dragontail, Cannon and Enchantment Peak on neighbouring days.
descent: A long day finishes down Aasgard Pass to Colchuck Lake, which is harder in this direction than coming up. Camped trips walk out down the Snow Creek drainage to the Snow Lakes trailhead.
logistics: The core zone is by overnight permit from an early-year lottery, with a few left for a same-day draw. The snowfield below The Prong can be icy early in the season. A car shuttle between the Colchuck and Snow Lakes trailheads makes a one-way traverse possible.
notes: One report did both in a single reverse thru-hike day (about 12 h, 8,000+ ft); the other did them on separate days from a Snow Lake zone camp (Little Annapurna day 2, McClellan day 3, via a gully on McClellan's northwest side). Only two pages read in full; a third (SummitPost four-peak weekend) was not fetched.
